evidence: Current source reads/edits and manual review. The cached reference archive was hashed and its class bytes decoded with a data-only Python reader; no Java classes were loaded. No builds, tests, syntax checks, project/game/renderer/JNI/shader/GPU execution, process inspection or exports. Runtime parity stays unverified by user instruction.

reference.phaseEvidence: java-simple-phase-source.json: supported cape/wing solid phase (0,0), skin model phase (0,7), base/bent custom phase (0,8) and glow custom phase (1,8). SimpleFeatureRenderPhase uses real RenderType reference keys and strictlyOrdered=false outputs, with retained clear/empty-order behavior.
reference.sortOnUpload: RenderSetup$RenderSetupBuilder.<init> writes sortOnUpload=false at 0x2a. RenderTypes.lambda$static$12 calls sortOnUpload at 0x15 for entityTranslucent; lambda$static$13 at 0x12 for entityTranslucentEmissive. The complete lambda$static$3 (entitySolid) and lambda$static$1 (armorCutoutNoCull) contain no such call.
reference.consolidation: RenderType.canConsolidateConsecutiveGeometry returns !primitiveTopology.connectedPrimitives. PrimitiveTopology.QUADS initializes connectedPrimitives=false. RenderPipelines ENTITY_SNIPPET selects QUADS at 0xf7; ENTITY_EMISSIVE_SNIPPET at 0x12d. This is distinct from the factory Boolean cache argument, which these translucent builders use for outline participation.
reference.preparedEqualityBoundary: The software renderer can compare its own actual bindings in a fixed frame. This does not establish Java PreparedRenderType equality for native GPU transform slices, output targets, scissor or texture descriptors.

collector.shared: JavaSimplePhases.Submit exposes an owned role, actual JavaRenderType object and reference model token. NativeAvatarGeometry.Batch implements it; Raster3D.SoftwareDraw supplies the same inputs for software. One implementation retains HashMap bucket traversal and clear/order lifetimes.
collector.preflight: Bound collections to 2048 submits. General/unknown roles, anonymous factory references, missing solid model boundaries, restarted model tokens or changed role/render reference inside a model invalidate known output. Reference identity is used for model tokens, not pose/coordinate equality. Results are bound to the exact WorldFrame and source container.
collector.independence: BedrockPlatform owns distinct native-packet and software collector instances. Software presentation does not drain packet history; geometry-only request failures do not reset software history. World/session gaps reset both. Software skips, surface mismatch and render-layer suppression reset software history; render rejection resets both.
collector.compatibility: Native packet collection still supplies the immutable geometry object and emits the same ARCGEO09/10 simple-phase trailer. No wire/archive/native ABI change.

software.entry: WorldFrame.render supplies its context and the dedicated software collector to Raster3D. Existing preview constructors keep their legacy path. Logical-ID sink overrides retain actual factory references for cape, wing, normal skin, base/glow cosmetics and bent skin.
software.submissions: Each sink retains its empty submit or clipped triangle list, source model token, pass, actual BufferedImage binding, blend and emissive state. Vertex attributes already contain pose/light/tint/overlay/fog variation; shader, projections, viewport and clipping rules are fixed for this raster frame. Changed prepared bindings inside a model make this owned phase path unavailable instead of being consolidated.
software.phaseOrder: Known complete owned simple inputs and declared sorting space draw solid phase (0,0), skin stage (0,7), custom base/bent (0,8), selected wing glint (1,7), and custom glow (1,8). Checked explicit views now support owned whole-skin model ordering (software-model-phase-source.json); missing views keep the older skin stage.
software.preparedDraws: Within each simple phase, traverse the collector's bucket/submission order and retain first prepared-binding encounter order. Reuse only this frame's actual image identity plus normalized shader pipeline, blend and emissive state; base and bent share their implemented pipeline. Keep empty submissions/first binding encounters and original model part/primitive order. No merge crosses a phase boundary.
software.quadSort: Solid cape/wing prepared draws retain primitive order. Checked base/bent and glow draws now request the stable descending projection-specific original quad key (software-projection-quad-sort-source.json). Missing context or any unknown key keeps the older comparator for that complete draw. Clipped triangles retain their source quad's key and stable equal-key order. The old global sort across incompatible materials is not used on this known path.
software.fallback: Unknown logical identities, general/unsupported variants, changed model bindings, undeclared sorting space or exceeding the 2048 staged-submit collector budget invalidate owned history and retain the existing renderer, including generic emissive behavior. Already-clipped staged triangles enter the legacy queues exactly once; subsequent sinks use those queues directly. No mesh re-emission, counter double-charge, geometry removal or anonymous RenderType identity is introduced. This fallback is not a parity/readiness assertion.
software.lifecycle: World-bound frames require complete quads at sink/model transitions and finish, and reject resuming an earlier sink. Finish seals collection before draining/drawing known phases; legacy fallback retains immediate solid rendering. Migration failure also seals/poisons the frame. Sealed frames reject later sinks/vertices and retrying partial finish; repeated successful finish returns the complete image without another drain. Existing preview reuse stays separate. Frame-local submissions/triangles clear after success; retained collector maps keep only owned factory references and cleared index lists.
software.budgets: At most 2048 staged sink records and the existing 2048 model-scope/200000 clipped-triangle caps, including glint. Larger sink collections use legacy rendering instead of imposing a new hard draw rejection. Prepared grouping uses identity image lookup plus bounded pipeline slots, and adds triangle references without copying pixels or re-emitting/skinning meshes. Runtime memory has not been measured.

remaining: Owned whole-skin sorting and supported projection-specific quad-key operators are now implemented for checked contexts (software-model-phase-source.json, software-projection-quad-sort-source.json). Actual native Java-equivalent pose/vertex-space provenance and complete model/raster equivalence remain unfinished or unverified.
